sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:141556
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 24332 of 2023

Applicant :- Achchhelal
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Om Prakash Gupta,Priyavrat Tripathi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Om Prakash Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
217 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kaptanganj,
District Kushinagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his bhabhi and according to the FIR,
marriage of the daughter of the informant was performed with the applicant on 9.6.2019 and after marriage, his daughter was tortured by applicant and his bhabhi for want of dowry and on 20.6.2021, his daughter informed him that she is being tortured by the applicant and his bhabhi and after information when he arrived at her matrimonial home then found that his daughter was lying dead.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is the husband of the deceased and on the basis of false and baseless allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present case.

5. He further submitted that although during investigation, informant and his witnesses stated against the applicant but when they appeared before the trial court then they were declared hostile and therefore, considering the fact that witnesses of facts including informant have already turned hostile and applicant who is in jail in the present case since 23.6.2021 i.e. for more than two years applicant may be released on bail.
6.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that post mortem report of the deceased suggests that deceased i.e. wife of the applicant died due to asphyxia as a result of throttling and therefore, it is a case of homicidal death and applicant failed to explain the death of his wife and therefore, merely on the ground that informant and other witnesses of fact have turned hostile, applicant who is husband of the deceased should not be released on bail.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Although, from the perusal of the record, it reflects that informant and some other witnesses of fact have turned hostile during trial before the trial court but applicant is husband of the deceased and post mortem report of the deceased shows that she died due to the throttling, therefore, it is a case of homicidal death and applicant who is husband of the deceased miserably failed to explain homicidal death of his wife.

9. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant who is husband of the deceased is not entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.

11. However, considering the fact that applicant is in jail in the present case for last two years, trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the case within a year from the date of production of certified copy of this order as per the provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C., if there is no legal impediment.

12. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 17.7.2023 Ankita  Achchhelal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137595241/
